newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Central Bank sees strong growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Central Bank sees strong growth in 97.

text.p: Sri Lanka Central Bank governor A.S. Jayawardena said on Friday he expected economic growth to accelerate to about six percent in 1997, up from less than four percent in 1996.
"We are hopeful that next year we will resume our trend path of growth, which is what we are expecting," Jayawardena told Reuters.
The government is targeting average growth of six percent for this Indian Ocean island. But heavy military spending and a severe power hit the economy in 1996.
"This year, we suffered a setback because we had a fairly severe drought and on top of it we had to have some power cuts in the middle of the year," Jayawardena said.
Hydroelectricity supplies almost 85 percent of Sri Lanka's power, but supplies were hit by a long drought.
"That I think has set the economy back this year to growth of about four percent," he said.

"Now, four percent growth is not a bad rate of growth, but for the Sri Lanka economy with a target of around six percent average, which we are planning, possibly more than six percent if the war is over, it's not good enough."
But Jaywardena also warned the country's power generation remained a concern.
"There are big doubts about this power. I am worried about this," he said.
"I have a feeling that they (power officials) are underestimating the growth in demand for power.

"There is no leeway in the power system -- you should always have some 20, 30 percent back-up in any power system. We are operating on the border. We have to move very fast in expanding the power capacity."
Power officials last week sought to reassure business leaders that there would be no repeat of the crippling power shortages in 1997.
The government, handing down its 1997 budget in November, projected Gross Domestic Product growth to rise to about 5.5 percent in 1997 from an estimated 3.7 percent in 1996.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga's reformist government, fighting an ethnic war against separatist Tamils, spent heavily on military procurement in 1996.
